confirmed.title: 'Only family-wise or market-first thresholds are usable' contradicted: pairwise at FPR 1e-4 matches the market-first PPV
confirmed.location: FINDINGS.md:43-45
confirmed.evidence: Quote: "pairwise screening at moderate thresholds has a PPV of a few percent at 1% coalition prevalence; only family-wise thresholds (above) or a market-first screen (PPV about 13% at 1% prevalence, 62% at 10%) are usable". e14/summary_N1M.json fpr1e-4/ppv_by_prevalence/0.01: v1 0.0846, v2_oneway 0.1056, v2_mutual 0.1349. The family-wise threshold recovers almost only XOR pairs (F2).
corrected: * **Precision at realistic prevalence**: precision depends mostly on how strict the threshold is, not on which screen is used. At 1% coalition prevalence (by market), pairwise screening at FPR 1e-3 has a PPV of 1-2%. At FPR 1e-4 it rises to 8-13% (48-61% at 10% prevalence). That matches the market-first screen at a market FPR of 1e-2 (about 13% at 1%, 62% at 10%). At a market FPR of 1e-3 the market-first screen reaches 38-54% at 1% prevalence. Each high-precision setting gives up recall: market-first recall is 7-15%, and pairwise recall at FPR 1e-4 is mostly XOR triads. The family-wise threshold reaches PPV of about 1 but recovers almost only XOR triads (recall 13-39%, other types at most 0.2%) (E14).

* **Precision at realistic prevalence**: PPV depends strongly on the threshold. With pairwise screening at a pair false-positive rate of 1e-3, PPV at 1% coalition prevalence is only 1.4-2.4%. At 1e-4 it rises to 8-13% (48-61% at 10% prevalence), but recall drops to mostly XOR triads plus some copy, lag and anti pairs. That is about the same as a market-first screen at a market false-positive rate of 1e-2 (PPV 13% at 1%, 62% at 10%, recall 13-15%). A stricter market screen (mFPR 1e-3) reaches a PPV of 38-54% at 1% prevalence, with recall of 7-10%. The family-wise threshold is almost free of false positives but recovers almost only XOR triads. At 1% prevalence, no threshold gives both high precision and broad recall.
